reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but shares only predicates for daily skipping rather than the complete occurrence-resolution policy.

duplication.why: Skip-versus-move orchestration is repeated across four consumers, and the holiday-dependent look-ahead formula is repeated in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs appropriately in shared/schedules.ts, but schedule eligibility and adjustment decisions remain distributed into server handlers and budget calculations.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling changes, their model data, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The small shared predicates help, but future scheduling-policy changes still require coordinating several resolution pipelines and independently maintained enumeration bounds.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts requests raw dates with getNextDate(..., true) and implements daily skipping locally; server/schedules/app.ts independently composes occurrence filtering and adjustment in both date handlers.

disguised_duplication.where: Daily non-working-day suppression appears as array filters in shared/schedules.ts and server/schedules/app.ts, but as a conditional budget increment plus a local resolveDate function in server/budget/schedule-template.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: A holidays parameter is added to applyWeekendRule, applyWeekendRuleToDay, and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; getNextDate gains a daily-skipping specialization, while createScheduleList, getUpcomingDates, and getDatesInRange independently implement that policy outside it.
